sections.title: Psychology
sections.intro: Psychology provides a supportive space to understand emotions, thoughts, behaviour and relationships. Therapy can help people develop practical coping strategies, self-awareness and confidence in navigating everyday challenges.

sections.title: Support built around everyday participation.
sections.intro: Therapy goals are individual. These examples show common areas that may be explored when they are relevant to the person and their priorities.

items.title: Emotional regulation
items.description: Understanding emotions and developing strategies to respond more effectively.

items.title: Anxiety & stress
items.description: Practical approaches for managing worry, stress and overwhelming situations.

items.title: Behaviour patterns
items.description: Understanding what may be driving behaviour and building more helpful responses.

items.title: Confidence & self-esteem
items.description: Supporting a stronger sense of capability, identity and self-belief.

items.title: Relationships
items.description: Building communication, boundaries and healthier ways of relating to others.

items.title: Coping & resilience
items.description: Developing tools for change, setbacks and everyday pressures.

panels.title: Goals first, service second.
paragraphs: Psychology support is tailored to the individual and is provided within the scope and availability of the treating clinician.
We start by understanding what is working well, what feels difficult and what meaningful change would look like in daily life. From there, the clinician can recommend a suitable next step.

items.title: Start with your priorities
items.description: Tell us what matters, what is currently difficult and what you hope to change.

items.title: Understand strengths & needs
items.description: Your clinician gathers relevant information and completes assessment where appropriate.

items.title: Build practical strategies
items.description: Sessions focus on meaningful goals and strategies that make sense in real routines.

items.title: Review & adapt
items.description: Progress is reviewed together and the plan is adjusted as needs and goals change.

sections.title: Before you get started.
sections.intro: These answers are general. We can discuss individual circumstances when you contact the team.

items.question: What should I expect from the first session?
items.answer: The first session is typically focused on understanding your current concerns, strengths, priorities and what you would like to change.

items.question: Is psychology only for crisis situations?
items.answer: No. People may seek psychology support for wellbeing, confidence, coping, relationships, behaviour or life changes as well as more significant concerns.

items.question: Can psychology work alongside other therapies?
items.answer: Yes. With appropriate consent, coordinated care can help different disciplines work toward compatible goals.
